# PLAN — iteration 1
## Current state assessment
The measured incumbent uses 4 LUTs and 5 FFs and meets setup (WNS 0.731 ns) and hold (WHS 0.191 ns); simulation and synthesis also pass. Since timing is already feasible and the objective is `minimize_luts`, a candidate must pass every deterministic gate and use fewer than 4 LUTs, or tie at 4 LUTs with fewer FFs, to improve the incumbent. Only `debouncer_top` is editable; its known top latency requires `// @latency 0`.

## Hypothesis
Inlining the child into the editable top and expressing the saturating three-bit stability counter as factored per-bit next-state equations may reduce the counter and terminal-detect logic by at least one LUT while retaining the same five state bits.

## Instruction for generator
Replace the transparent `debouncer` instance with equivalent top-level sequential logic, retaining `clean`, the sampled input, and the three-bit stability count with synchronous active-high reset. Factor the count update into per-bit increment/toggle equations with explicit mismatch-to-one and terminal-count hold behavior, so synthesis can share the terminal detection instead of rebuilding separate increment and equality mux logic. Preserve the first changed sample as count 1, update `clean` on the eighth consecutive matching sample, and keep `clean` unchanged otherwise; retain `// @latency 0`.
